text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Oslo on Monday. Arafat said his visit to Norway was important for the Middle East peace process and that he was not here to waste time. American and Israeli authorities have criticised the Palestinian leader for leaving the Middle East during negotiations between Palestinian and Israeli officials.
- Thirty-nine percent of Norwegian households own a personnel computer, according to a market survey commissioned by Compaq Computer Norway.

- Telecommunications company Nera presented a weaker result for the first nine-months of 1996 than expected. Pre-tax profits of 90.3 million crowns were seven percent lower than during the same period last year.

- Scandinavian Airline System (SAS) increased its share of the domestic Norwegian market by almost two percent in September to 42.5 percent compared with its biggest competitor Braathens SAFE. This was SAS' largest share of the domestic market since it was deregulated in December 1994.

- Swedish furniture company IKEA will spend 300-400 million crowns to build a new store at Furuset in the Norwegian capital Oslo. The company had to strike a complicated deal with the local community involving the building of a new 60-70 million crown sports club to get its prefered site.
